text:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate + tail latency spike for inference cluster az1a. Affected fleet: ephemeral-worker-* (g5x). Start time ~2026-03-17T14:02Z. See metrics: https://grafana.redwood/az1a/inference/errors

elaine: acked. paging oncall. i'm pulled in. observability shows rps steady but p95 CPU and grpc errors climbing.

matt: i'm seeing per-host connection queues backed up, accept queue depth growing on several hosts. kernel TX queue also elevated on az1a.

sre-jordan: any signs of autoscaler thrashing? or too many concurrent requests per ephemeral instance?

elaine: autoscaler stable. suspect concurrency limit + KV cache pressure causing stalls. 502s correlate with hosts hitting >600 concurrent streams.

eng-runtime-ryan: confirmed. new load test earlier increased model concurrency knobs; some hosts have large accept backlog and grpc keepalives piling up. recommending temporary concurrency cap rollback and enabling overflow routing.

matt: putting a quick mitigation in place: set route policy for az1a inference pool to reduce max_concurrency_per_host from 600 -> 300. Applying now: `curl -XPOST https://controlplane/api/routes/az1a/patch -d '{"max_concurrency":300}'`

incident-bot: deploy job started: route-config-update-5623456789. CI check passed. Rolling to 100% in 30s.

elaine: rolling back concurrency improved accept queues on first 8 hosts. p50/p95 latencies dropping. but a subset still showing high kernel tx delays. those hosts may have NIC/driver hysteresis.

eng-runtime-ryan: plan B in parallel: enable cross-region fallback for new sessions to eu-west1 for non-SLA customers and throttle retries. Adding traffic weighting: az1a-> 70%, eu-west1->30% for default inference route.

matt: configured fallback weighting. traffic shift in progress. watch for increased cold-starts in eu-west.

cust-success-raj: heads up — we've noticed a few paying customers hitting 5xx from 14:05Z. I'm drafting an incident advisory for customers impacted in az1a with mitigation steps.

elaine: good. customer comm: say we observed transient instance-level network/concurrency degradation in az1a, mitigation active (traffic steering + concurrency cap). Recommend retry/backoff and optional region pin to eu-west for critical workloads.

eng-runtime-ryan: also performing rolling restarts of 12 suspected hosts to clear NIC state. Using drain -> restart -> verify pattern: `for h in $(list-hosts); do drain $h; restart $h; wait-health $h; done`

incident-bot: host-restart job created: restart-batch-az1a-5623456789. Will run 5 hosts at a time. ETA ~20m.

matt: first restart batch finished. three hosts recovered, tx-sched delays resolved on them. overall error rate down from 6.3% -> 1.1%.

elaine: handing off to night oncall @sre-jordan in 15m. current status: concurrency cap applied, cross-region fallback enabled, rolling restarts ongoing, customer advisory drafted. Remaining action items logged in runbook: https://wiki.redwood/incident-runbooks/az1a-concurrency-deg

sre-jordan: taking over. will monitor for 2 hours then close if stable. pls ping if any regression. :white_check_mark:

cust-success-raj: customer advisory sent to affected accounts at 14:28Z. included temporary region recommendations and ETA for follow-up.

elaine: noted. final note before handoff: suspected root cause likely combination of increased allowed concurrency + ephemeral NIC scheduling edgecase. follow-up: validate default concurrency knobs and add kernel tx metrics to synthetic alarms.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation reduced customer-facing errors to <1%. Rolling restarts 9/12 complete. Next update scheduled in 30m.
